request.spec:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.
request.prompt:

DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sorting works and the main "sorting" test passes. Two of the four tests in the spec still fail, and in both cases the spec expects something no app could produce.

**Results of the last `bin/e2e` run**
- ✓ `sorting`: the main test for this change.
- ✓ `sorting scenario 2`
- ✘ `sorting scenario 1`, at `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:219` (and again at line 302). It expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p`. The app shows the real id (`smvk8lgq2p08e-p`). The `__SHEET__` placeholder was never filled in with the test's sheet id.
- ✘ `sorting scenario 3`, at `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:932`. It looks up Fay's row by the name "Fay", then expects that row to show Ada's name, grade, claims and tags. Line 1033 expects the same row to show "Fay", with no rename in between. The checks are written against the wrong person.

Neither scenario uses the sort. I didn't edit the spec, so those two will keep failing until someone fixes it.

**What I changed**
- **Sort select** (`sort-by`, options added / name / grade / due-total): it sits above the people list.
  - Your choice is kept in the page address, so it stays when you reload a sheet and doesn't affect other users.
  - Name ignores case and surrounding spaces, the same way names are compared elsewhere. Grade uses the grade in force on the sheet's today. Due-total sorts by the figure shown on the row, lowest first, with n/a last.
  - People with equal keys keep their list order.
- **Display only:** the sort only reorders the rows on screen. Positions, rollup lines and bulk actions still work from the stored list order. The sorting code is in a new file, `features/people/sort.ts`, wired into `people.slot.tsx`. I also exported `toCents` from `rates.ts` so the sort can reuse it.
- **Loading fix:** loading a sheet now fetches its people before the sheet id appears on screen (`SheetPicker.tsx`, using a new `peopleQuery` in `people.ts`). Before this, a second user who had just signed in could read the list while it was still empty, which failed the main test.

**Port clash:** I ran the tests with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`. Your shell sets `PORT=3002`, and a Java process that has been up about two hours, probably another sandbox's copy of this app, already holds that port. The app couldn't start there, so the first runs failed for that reason alone. I left that process running.
